quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts.
Give yourself extra space when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it rains. Your tires are driving on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain or when water is on the road. This helps your wheels keep traction.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to react to dangers on the road. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look at the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: To be safe when crossing a railroad, you should:

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways before crossing.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways before crossing.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions before crossing the tracks. Wait for signals to clear and be certain it is safe before you cross.

questions.question: A sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph" means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. When a new speed limit is shown on these signs, the new limit starts right at the sign.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle only half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give a motorcyclist a full lane width. They need room to move safely, even if there seems to be extra space in the lane.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: You may carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If a yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection, continue through carefully.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive through it.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive through it.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot completely cross. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash through it means:

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: Some regulatory signs forbid certain actions. These signs are white and rectangular with red and black markings. A red circle with a slash over a black symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you pass. This gives other drivers time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is safe.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches for what other drivers might do and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: Both vehicles need half of the road each. This gives both drivers enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn tires make it harder to turn, take longer to stop, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause more fatal crashes. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because it can make other drivers impatient and cause them to take unsafe actions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road curves sharply to the left. You may see several of these signs along the curve.
